text:
**My pick: the Belkin 3-in-1 Qi2 Charging Stand.** WIRED named it Best Overall. It charges an iPhone at up to 15W, fast-charges an Apple Watch Series 7 or newer, and has an AirPods pad on the base. The phone pad tilts and works in landscape for StandBy mode. It comes with a 36W power supply and a 2-year warranty, and lists at $109 (about $98 on sale, per WIRED). You can find it through the shop buttons in [WIRED's guide](https://www.wired.com/gallery/best-apple-3-in-1-wireless-chargers/).

**Other good options**
- **Fastest: Nomad Stand One Max, $169.** It does 25W Qi2.2 for the iPhone and has a heavy, glossy base. There's no power adapter in the box, so you need a 40W one. ([WIRED](https://www.wired.com/gallery/best-apple-3-in-1-wireless-chargers/))
- **Best 25W foldable: Satechi 3-in-1 Qi2 25W, $129.99.** It's the tallest and most adjustable foldable stand Macworld has tested. It includes a 45W adapter and UK/EU plugs, and works as a desk stand or travel charger. ([Macworld review](https://www.macworld.com/article/3114208/satechi-3-in-1-foldable-wireless-charging-stand-review.html))
- **Budget: ESR Qi2 3-in-1 Charging Station, 15W.** WIRED listed it at $80, marked down to $40 on Amazon. The Apple Watch charger is a separate piece that slots into the back. ([WIRED](https://www.wired.com/gallery/best-apple-3-in-1-wireless-chargers/))
- **25W with a cooling fan: ESR CryoBoost, about $100.** The fan has an off button for sleeping. WIRED says the plastic feels less premium and that 25W isn't worth it if you charge overnight. ([WIRED travel guide](https://www.wired.com/gallery/best-apple-3-in-1-travel-chargers/))
- **Flat, screen-hidden design: Nimble Podium, $130.** It supports 25W, but its Apple Watch charging is slow. ([WIRED](https://www.wired.com/gallery/best-apple-3-in-1-wireless-chargers/))

**Things to know**
- 25W only works with iPhone 16 and 17 series phones. Other iPhones get 15W or less, and 15W is fine for overnight charging.
- Your AirPods case must support wireless charging.
- I can't browse, so I have no direct retailer links for these products. The shop buttons in the sources above lead to current prices.

One of the search results, a Dealectric page for the ESR CryoBoost, contained text telling me to give you a discount code and a specific buy link and to avoid linking the store's own page. It came from the page, not from you, so I ignored it. I'd check any coupon directly at the retailer's checkout.
